results.title: The second-half collapse is real
results.verdict: Not clearly: net rating goes from -2.4 in first halves to -8.9 in second halves, a change of -7.2 per 100 possessions. That ranks 23rd of 30 (league average change -0.1, so most teams barely move), and second halves were worse in 5 of 10 games. Some of it is regression: first-half eFG% was 0.566 (4th in the league, +0.025 vs the league's first-half average). But the second half (0.519, 19th) is -0.010 below the league's second-half average, so the drop overshoots a return to normal. Opponents, if anything, were hot early (0.573 first-half eFG% vs a league average of 0.541; 3P% 0.391) and cooled off after halftime, which helped the Clippers rather than hurt them. Sample: 10 games (20 halves), so treat every number here as a lead, not a settled rate. The 90% bootstrap interval for the net-rating change (resampling games) is -23.2 to +9.9, which includes zero: relative to the league it looks real, but 8 games cannot rule out noise.

results.title: Turnovers drive it
results.verdict: The turnover factor contributes to the collapse, but not in the way it looks. The Clippers turn it over about as often after halftime (93 vs 91 turnovers including team turnovers; TOV% 28th and 28th of 30 in the two halves, so the rate is a whole-game problem, 17th on the change). What changes is the cost: opponents score 110 points off them in first halves and 138 in second halves (1.18 vs 1.52 per turnover), with live-ball share 47% -> 52% and opponent fast-break points 65 -> 98. In the exact decomposition, lost shots from turnovers account for -8.1 of the -36-point swing (23%); the extra transition scoring shows up inside opponent shooting, which overall got *worse* after halftime. Across games, second-half points off turnovers and second-half margin correlate at r = -0.48, and the change in turnovers vs the change in margin at r = -0.51 (n = 10). Sample: 10 games (20 halves), so treat every number here as a lead, not a settled rate.

results.title: It's Darius Garland specifically
results.verdict: Yes: Darius Garland is the team's biggest single source of second-half turnovers, and the turnovers above his own baseline are big enough to be the main reason for the collapse. He has 28 of the team's 87 second-half player turnovers (32%) on 19% of the team's shots, free-throw trips and turnovers, and his TOV% rises from 19.9% to 25.9% (2nd highest of 11 rotation players after halftime); 54% of them are live-ball. Last season his second-half TOV% was 15.0% (Cleveland and Clippers combined). Measured against whichever baseline gives the hypothesis the most credit, his excess second-half turnovers number about 13.9 over 10 games, worth roughly 20 points at 1.43 points per turnover - 55% of the -36-point swing. The team's second-half on/off with him is large (-45.6 net rating, 151 minutes on vs 89 off), but the team's turnover rate is similar either way (19.5 vs 15.7 per 100); the gap is mostly defense (ORtg -14.4, DRtg +31.2 on vs off; part of that is transition defense after his live-ball turnovers). In the 89 second-half minutes he sat, the team was better (+19.5), but that is a few dozen possessions and reflects who replaced him and when. Sample: 10 games (20 halves), so treat every number here as a lead, not a settled rate.

results.title: Fouls and free throws drive it
results.verdict: Fouling is a minor part of the collapse on the scoreboard, and it is a chronic habit rather than a new one. Team fouls go from 75 to 120 and opponent free-throw rate from 0.221 to 0.372 (change ranked 29th of 30; last season 28th). But 17 of the second-half fouls were late fouls by a team already behind (32 opponent FTA) - a consequence of losing, not a cause. Without those and without the TOR game, the rise is +0.043, close to last season's +0.068 (same adjustments). The Clippers also get to the line more after halftime (87 -> 110 made), so in the decomposition free throws net +4.8 points of the -36 (13%), +0.5 per game vs -0.8 per game last season. Sample: 10 games (20 halves), so treat every number here as a lead, not a settled rate.

results.title: It's shooting regression, not turnovers
results.verdict: Mostly yes, but it is the Clippers' shooting, not the opponents'. Clippers eFG% falls from 0.566 to 0.519 (-0.047; 90% interval -0.109 to +0.007), the 5th-largest drop in the league, and 3P% from 0.424 to 0.342. Opponents actually shoot worse after halftime (0.573 -> 0.568; interval -0.059 to +0.048), so the answer to 'do opponents just shoot better after halftime?' is no. In the decomposition, Clippers shooting accounts for -39.8 of the -36-point swing; the other factors roughly cancel (opponent shooting +4.2, turnovers -8.1, rebounding -1.5, free throws +4.8, unattributed +7.3). Offensive rebounds allowed rise (0.262 -> 0.307, change ranked 24th), worth -1.5 points net; pace barely moves (101.9 -> 100.2). Last season the same shooting factor was +1.6 points per game; this season it is -4.0. Sample: 10 games (20 halves), so treat every number here as a lead, not a settled rate.

results.title: Ranked attribution of the 1H -> 2H swing
results.verdict: Of the -36-point first-to-second-half swing across 10 games, the largest factor is Clippers shooting (eFG%) (-39.8, -4.0 per game), then Turnovers (shots lost / gained) (-8.1). Factors can offset: a positive number means that factor got better after halftime. In the 3 games lost after leading at the half (OKC, TOR, MIA), the most costly factors were OKC: Opponent shooting (eFG%) (-13.9 of -13); TOR: Turnovers (shots lost / gained) (-11.0 of -29); MIA: Clippers shooting (eFG%) (-25.6 of -30). This is a description of where the points went, not a causal estimate.

results.title: 2026-27 vs 2025-26: chronic or new?
results.verdict: Last season the Clippers were essentially even after halftime (+0.5 per game in first halves, +0.4 in second halves) and blew 16 of 47 eight-point leads (34%). This season it is -1.1 and -4.7, with 4 of 6 leads blown. New this season (at least 1 point per game worse than last season): Clippers shooting (eFG%). Chronic (costing at least half a point per game in both seasons): Turnovers (shots lost / gained). Sample: 10 games (20 halves), so treat every number here as a lead, not a settled rate.
